llm.summary: The skill's instructions mostly match a local-publisher purpose, but it references undeclared credentials/config paths and fallbacks (e.g., ACP admin API key, control plane URL, and a local config file) and assumes tooling that is not included — these inconsistencies warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description claim a local Naver Blog publisher that uses a buyer-local runner and one-time browser login. That is coherent with the runtime steps (doctor, login, publish). However the SKILL.md also mentions control-plane fallbacks (CONTROL_PLANE_URL + ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY) and multiple runtime env/config keys that are not declared in the registry metadata, which is unexpected for a pure local publisher.

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to run npx commands, start a local daemon, and optionally load X_LOCAL_TOKEN from ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json. The skill will therefore access a local config path and run external packages. The skill also references tools under openclaw/skill-pack/... which are not present in this package — the agent may try to execute commands or read files outside the skill bundle. These file/env accesses were not declared in the skill metadata.

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only. This is lower installation risk, but the instructions rely on an external npm package (@y80163442/naver-thin-runner) fetched at runtime via npx; that external package is where code execution risk actually lives.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The registry lists no required env vars, but SKILL.md references multiple runtime variables and tokens (SETUP_URL, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, X_LOCAL_TOKEN). Some (X_LOCAL_TOKEN, local config) are reasonable for a local runner, but CONTROL_PLANE_URL + ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY are powerful and unrelated to simply publishing a single blog post and are not declared — this is disproportionate and should be justified before use.

Note: autonomous invocation + the ability to call external tools could increase impact if the external tools are malicious, but that is not a unique flag here.

llm.guidance: This skill is instruction-only and appears intended to use a local macOS 'thin-runner' (npm package @y80163442/naver-thin-runner) to publish posts from an authenticated local browser. Before installing or using it: 1) Verify the npm package and its publisher (@y80163442) — npx will download and run code on your machine. 2) Confirm you are comfortable the tool will read ~/.config/naver-thin-runner/config.json (it may load a local session token). 3) Ask why the skill mentions CONTROL_PLANE_URL + ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY as a fallback — do not provide an ACP admin key unless you fully trust the offering; that key could grant broad control. 4) Note the skill references local tools under openclaw/skill-pack that are not included; ask where those come from and who runs them. 5) Prefer running the setup/login commands manually and inspecting what the npm package does (or run in an isolated environment) before giving it access to any credentials or your main machine.
